As an application, we prove that if $M$ is a simple infinite-dimensional $\mathfrak{g}$-module with the minimal GK dimension on which $f-1$ acts locally nilpotently, then $M\cong P\otimes V$ for some simple $\mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1$-module $P$ and some finite-dimensional simple $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$-module $V$. We also give a new proof of the Skryabine quivalence and Petukhov's birational decomposition of the quotient division ring of $U(\mathfrak{g})$.

papers.title: Selected character moments, zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions over number fields, and Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain a zero-free half-plane $\Rea s>B_2$ for every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over every number field, where \[ B_2=\frac{777-\sqrt{1081}}{852} =0.873381966613207519929\ldots. \] We adapt selected character-sum estimates and finite moment inductions to ideal-character sums over arbitrary number fields and restore ordinary sixth powers. Two finite moment inductions give an ordinary product estimate with length condition $n_1+n_2+2z\le M$ for sufficiently fine original prime factors. Applying this estimate to zero detection and the averaged numerator in the cubic-theta comparison gives the stated boundary. We determine the exact infimum of the resulting comparison system and verify its scalar inequalities by rational Bernstein bounds. The proof uses the earlier theta, moment and continuation theorems over number fields.

papers.title: Serre modularity over real quadratic fields
papers.abstract: Assuming GRH for Dedekind zeta functions, we prove Serre’s conjecture over the real quadratic fields \(\mathbf Q(\sqrt d)\) for \[ d\in\{2,3,5,6,7,10,11,13,17,21,33,37,41,57,65,73,89\}. \] More precisely, every continuous, absolutely irreducible, totally odd two-dimensional Galois representation over these fields in odd residual characteristic is modular. The result for \(d=17\) is unconditional; for \(d=33\), GRH can be replaced by the assertion that Dedekind zeta functions have no zeros with real part greater than \(31/32\). The proof combines conductor reduction with local ramification estimates and global discriminant bounds. Its principal new ingredients are a modularity criterion for \(2\)-adic representations with scalar reduction and integral trace arguments that force quadratic descent or bound coefficient fields. Uniform local lifting constructions allow these methods to treat arbitrary conductor.

papers.title: Stable equivalence of quadratic monomial algebras
papers.abstract: It is well known that gentle algebras are closed under derived equivalence. However, it is easy to verify that they are not closed under stable equivalence. We prove that the classes of quadratic monomial, almost gentle and string almost gentle algebras are closed under stable equivalence. In fact, in each of these cases, stable equivalence is characterized by isomorphism after deleting all nodes and removing semisimple direct summands. The underlying isomorphism theorem gives a positive answer to Mart\'inez-Villa's question on selfinjective-free algebras for these classes. We also prove that the nonprojective simple modules form the unique weakly simple-minded system of a quadratic monomial algebra. Consequently, every stable equivalence of Morita type involving such an algebra lifts to a Morita equivalence when neither algebra has semisimple direct summands. Finally, we describe the effect of node deletion on stable categories of Gorenstein-projective modules and singularity categories, and give combinatorial descriptions of the equivalences for almost gentle algebras using marked configurations.

papers.title: The exact multiplicity of the Wilson supercongruence in F_q[t]
papers.abstract: Let q = p^s with p an odd prime, and let P be a monic irreducible polynomial of degree d >= 2 in F_q[t]. The Wilson analogue F_d = -1 mod P holds for the product F_d of all nonzero polynomials of degree less than d, and Thakur proved that P is a Wilson prime, i.e. F_d = -1 mod P^2, exactly when all exponents of P are congruent to 0 or 1 mod p, in which case the congruence holds modulo P^(p-1). He asked whether it can hold modulo a higher power, and what the exact multiplicities are. Let r be the largest integer such that all exponents of P are congruent to 0 or 1 modulo p^r. We prove that the exact multiplicity m = v_P(F_d + 1) is 1 if r = 0, p^r - 1 if 1 <= r <= s, and q + 1 if r > s. In particular m <= q + 1, and the multiplicity of a Wilson prime in the numerator of the sum over i < d of 1/(t^(q^i) - t) is exactly m - 1. Examples over F_3, F_5 and F_9 show that all regimes occur. A script checks the theorem on all primes of small degree and on these examples.

papers.title: The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$
papers.abstract: Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\CH(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations. The ring $\CH(\mathcal M_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, with five relations. In particular, we find that the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle, $\lambda_3$, has order 504 on $\mathcal A_3$ and 252 on $\mathcal M_3$. For $\mathcal A_3$, this removes the factor of 4 from the bound $252\mid\operatorname{ord}(\lambda_3)\mid 1008$ of Ekedahl and van der Geer.

papers.title: The p-adic valuations of the coefficients in Yang's expansion of (1+1/x)^x
papers.abstract: Yang's coefficients b_n, defined by (1+1/x)^x = e(1 - sum_{n>=1} b_n (x+1)^{-n}), appear in refinements of Carleman's inequality, and the literature on them concerns their analytic properties. We study their p-adic valuations for an odd prime p. From the identity 1 - sum_n b_n u^n = exp(-sum_{k>=1} u^k/(k(k+1))) one gets v_p(b_n) >= -M(n), where M(n) is the optimum of a knapsack problem on the compositions of n. We compute M(n) in closed form and show that, for n >= 2, the optimum is attained by a unique composition exactly when n = (p-1)m with m in an explicit set U_p defined by a digit condition. For these n the bound is an equality: v_p(b_n) = -(m + v_p(m!)). The set U_p has density 1/(p-1), so the valuation of b_n is determined on a set N_p of indices of density 1/(p-1)^2. The set N_p contains the indices p^K - 1, at which b_{p^K-1} is the unique coefficient of minimal valuation among b_1, ..., b_{p^K-1}. The same statements hold for the coefficients of e(1-u)^{1/u}, and the minimality statement for those of e(1-u)^{1/u-1}. A script checks all statements numerically in finite ranges.

papers.title: The Pila-Zannier strategy for Drinfeld modules and Drinfeld modular curves
papers.abstract: We extend the Pila-Zannier strategy to Drinfeld modules: we prove analogues of the Manin-Mumford theorem for a product of two Drinfeld modules of equal rank, and of the Andr\'e-Oort theorem for a product of two Drinfeld modular curves. In characteristic zero, several steps of this strategy rest on $o$-minimality, which has no counterpart over a function field; we replace the counting step by the rigid analytic Pila-Wilkie theorem of Binyamini-Kato, and this appears to be its first arithmetic application. The functional transcendence input, namely an analogue of the Ax-Lindemann theorem in both settings, is established here by an independent point counting argument.

papers.title: The pliability of del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We study $G$-Mori fibre space models of $G$-del Pezzo surfaces, focusing on surfaces over non-closed fields. We construct explicit examples of birationally rigid sextic del Pezzo surfaces and give a negative answer to a generalization of Koll\'ar's question on birational rigidity and field extensions: a sextic del Pezzo surface of Picard rank $1$ can fail to be birationally rigid over its ground field but become birationally rigid after an algebraic field extension. We interpret this phenomenon in terms of the failure of injectivity of natural maps in nonabelian Galois cohomology induced by the inclusion of automorphism groups into birational automorphism groups. We also show that finite pliability is unbounded: for every integer $d\geqslant2$, we construct a sextic del Pezzo surface of index $3$ over a field of characteristic zero whose pliability is exactly $3^d+1$.

papers.title: The super Weil-Petersson asymptotic expansion and the coefficients
papers.abstract: We determine the universal constant in the large-genus asymptotic expansion of super Weil-Petersson volumes. The argument adopts the uniform-transport strategy for shifted theta intersection numbers. The uniform large-genus theorem for normalized BGW numbers of Guo-Norbury-Yang-Zagier determines the amplitude at a simpler endpoint. The result is $C=\pi^{-9/2}$. We give a proof of the Griguolo-Papalini-Russo-Seminara conjecture for fixed boundary lengths and fixed descendant degrees. The boundary formula is uniform when the sum of the lengths is $o(\sqrt g)$, and we exhibit an obstruction at the $\sqrt g$ scale. We also compute the first four inverse-genus coefficients by two exact recursive methods and derive general polynomial structure results. Finally, we show that, for each fixed genus, the super Weil-Petersson volume divided by $n!$ is a polynomial in the number $n$ of marked points.

papers.title: The Zelevinsky involution, co-standard modules for quantum affine algebras and interval symmetric functions
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathscr{F}_n$ be the subcategory of finite-dimensional representations of the quantum loop algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ whose simple modules are indexed by multisegments consisting of intervals $[a,b]$, where $a,b$ are integers and $0<b-a\le n$. We define the co-standard module associated to a multisegment $\mathbf{s}$ to be the tensor product of the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules, associated to the first node of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$, given by the segments of $\mathbf{s}$. Under a suitable (and necessary) restriction on $n$, we show that its socle is isomorphic to the simple module given by the Zelevinsky dual $\mathbf{s}^\dagger$ of $\mathbf{s}$. We then define an involution $\Phi$ of the Grothendieck ring $\mathcal{K}(\mathscr {F}_n)$ and prove that it maps the class of a simple module to the class of the simple module given by its Zelevinsky dual. We also show that on suitable subcategories $\Phi$ is induced by an exact autoequivalence reversing tensor products, and we give a $t$-analogue of the multiplicity identity in the quantum Grothendieck ring.
  Motivated by the determinantal formula for alternating snake modules, we realize $\mathcal{K}(\mathscr {F}_n)$ explicitly inside a polynomial ring in variables indexed by intervals, and, in the spirit of Macdonald's ninth variation of Schur functions, we show that the fundamental modules correspond to analogues of the elementary symmetric functions and the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules to analogues of the complete homogeneous symmetric functions. This is compatible with $\Phi$ and the classical involution $\omega$, and we prove that alternating snake modules give a family of Schur positive symmetric functions extending the skew Schur functions.

papers.title: Three-colour solutions from four-colour cubes
papers.abstract: For every $n\ge2$, any $16n-3$ cubes, each using all four colours of a fixed palette, contain an $n\times n\times n$ frame whose exterior faces are monochromatic in exactly three colours; this bound is sharp. For a fixed palette, exactly two collections of $16n-4$ cubes fail, and reflection exchanges them. For $n\ge3$, every failure of size at least $14n$ lies in one ordinary orientation class with four bounded colour buckets. This gives $2\binom{d+15}{15}$ failures at size $16n-4-d$, for $0\le d\le2n-4$, of which $2\binom{d+11}{11}$ are inclusion-maximal. The threshold for a complete cube is $\max\{n^3,16n-3\}$; in particular, any $n^3$ source cubes suffice when $n\ge4$. The case $n=2$ answers the threshold question in Problem 2 of Berkove, Eickemeyer and Schulman (2018). The proof combines their corner-containment reduction with orientation constraints and double counting.

papers.title: Torsion of elliptic curves over number fields of degree $6$, $7$, $8$ and $9$
papers.abstract: We determine all the groups that appear as the torsion group of an elliptic curve over a number field of degree $d$ for $d=6$, $7$, $8$ and $9$. Apart from the groups that occur infinitely often, exactly $4$ groups occur in degree $6$, $3$ in degree $7$, $8$ in degree $8$ and $9$ in degree $9$, and among them the groups $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ over sextic fields, $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/15\mathbb{Z}$ over octic fields and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/26\mathbb{Z}$ over nonic fields were not known to occur. For $13$ of these $24$ pairs of a degree and a group we also determine all the elliptic curves that realize them. The proofs combine the global method of Derickx, Hecke sieves, formal immersion criteria at the prime $2$ with Hecke operators, and Riemann-Roch computations on modular curves and their quotients over finite fields.

papers.title: Turán's pure power sum problem: certified bounds for finite $n$ and $\limsup R_n\le 0.68637$
papers.abstract: For $n\ge1$ let $R_n=\inf\max_{1\le k\le n}|z_1^k+\dots+z_n^k|$, the infimum being over all complex $z_1=1,z_2,\dots,z_n$. This is Turán's pure power sum problem (Erdős problem #519). The best published upper bound for the constant $\limsup R_n$ is $0.69368$, from a computation of Harcos reported by Biró in 2000. We prove $\limsup_{n\to\infty}R_n\le0.68637$. The construction is the Biró–Harcos linearization, with the first half of the power sums prescribed as $s_k=Te^{i\varphi(k/n)}$ for a piecewise-linear phase $\varphi$ that varies from the start. We prove a limit theorem: the quantity that controls the second half converges to an explicit functional of the solution of a linear Volterra equation whose associated operator is a contraction. The resulting inequality is certified in ball arithmetic by an a posteriori error bound, with two separately written programs that follow the same mathematical argument. We also give rigorous upper bounds for $R_n$ at 13 values of $n$ between $300$ and $10^6$, from explicit exact certificates, each checked by one or two programs written independently of the generator. In an appendix, R. Pinho applies the limit theorem to a finer profile, with sharper error bounds, and certifies $\limsup R_n\le0.6863607950$. The work was done with substantial help from AI models; it has not been refereed.

papers.title: Uniform comparison of multiplier and test ideals for polynomials with affinely independent support
papers.abstract: Let $f\in\Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ have affinely independent exponent vectors. We prove that its test ideals agree with the reductions of its multiplier ideals at all nonnegative real exponents for every sufficiently large prime in one arithmetic progression. The progression depends only on the support of $f$.

papers.title: Uniform irreducibility and Galois groups of generalized Laguerre polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that the generalized Laguerre polynomial $H_{n,s}$ is irreducible over $\mathbb Q$ and has Galois group containing $A_n$ for every positive integer $s$, once $n$ exceeds an effective absolute constant. Equivalently, every numerator and denominator in the exponential Pad\'e table has these properties once its own degree is sufficiently large. The exceptional positive integral pairs form an effectively computable finite set. The proof combines integral traces at degenerate fibers, Pad\'e resultants, and an energy inequality for Galois-invariant positive semidefinite forms on the roots.

papers.title: Uniform localization and boundary corrections for two-node quiver Coulomb branches
papers.abstract: We construct simple coherent classes and compute their normalized difference operators for the two-node quiver Coulomb branch with gauge group $GL_1\times GL_2$ and $m-1$ framing columns at the second node. The first magnetic charge is fixed at zero. For every $m\geq1$, every support $(n,-1)$ with $n\geq1$, and every integral electric twist, we prove that termwise saturation of the matter Koszul complex gives the simple intermediate extension. A graded normalization formula expresses its localization on every stratum as a finite binomial shuffle sum. The resulting operators satisfy bar symmetry, positive bubbling order, paired root-residue cancellation, and integral Laurent polynomial action. For $m=4$, we construct the derived boundary correction on $(2,-2)$, retaining the nonsemisimple odd-electric boundary object, and compute all electric twists. Finally, matter Euler divisibility proves triangular uniqueness on arbitrary fixed rank-two magnetic supports inside the actual integral Coulomb image. A pole-free counterexample shows why residue conditions alone do not give this uniqueness. Existence on general deeper mixed-sign supports remains open.

papers.title: Weierstrass semigroups at totally ramified places of degree one on generalized Kummer extensions
papers.abstract:
We explicitly describe the set of gaps and the Weierstrass semigroup at a totally ramified place of degree one on a generalized Kummer extension defined by the affine equation $y^m = f(x)$ over $K$, an algebraic extension of $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $f(x)\in K(x)$ and $K$ is not required to contain a primitive $m$-th root of unity.
  For the different totally ramified places of degree one, our description takes a unified form.
  Then we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for the Weierstrass semigroup at a totally ramified place of degree one to be symmetric.
  Furthermore, we investigate the minimal generating set of the Weierstrass semigroups at many totally ramified places of degree one.
  We not only explicitly describe the minimal generating set, but also provide functions whose coefficients of pole divisors lie in the minimal generating set.
  Finally, we apply our results to generalized Kummer extensions with the same multiplicities, as well as function fields of GGS curves and subcovers of the BM curve.
